The Burden of Leadership

Chief Adeolu had always coveted the throne. For years, he had plotted and schemed, forming alliances with the most unsavory characters in the village. When the old king finally joined his ancestors, Adeolu’s path seemed clear. However, the crown was heavier than he anticipated. The village was plagued by drought, the youths were restless, and the treasury was empty. The very people who had cheered his ascension now grumbled in market squares. Adeolu realized too late that power was not just about wearing royal robes and eating from silver platters; it was a burden that demanded wisdom, sacrifice, and the ability to listen—virtues he had never cultivated. His nights became sleepless, haunted by the realization that he was a king in title but a pauper in leadership.

content:
The Impact of Artificial Intelligence

Artificial Intelligence (AI) is no longer the stuff of science fiction; it is weaving itself into the fabric of daily life. From recommendation algorithms on streaming services to sophisticated diagnostic tools in healthcare, AI is ubiquitous. Proponents argue that it increases efficiency and solves complex problems faster than the human brain. However, critics raise ethical concerns regarding privacy, bias in algorithms, and the potential displacement of jobs. As machines become smarter, the line between human intuition and machine logic blurs. The challenge for the 21st century is not just developing AI, but governing it to ensure it serves humanity rather than enslaving it.
